reviews.text: Ryan Coogler is quickly rising the ranks as one of my favorite directors working today. He arguably gives us the best film in the Rocky franchise, and it’s the saga’s seventh installment.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Michael B. Jordan is a star, and Sylvester Stallone turns his most iconic character of Rocky Balboa into one of the best supporting performances of the year.
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: Just when you were thinking: How long can Rocky keep fighting, this detour that introduces a new character, the illegitimate son of Apollo Creed, Adonis Creed, and brings fresh blood to stain the ring. A good transition for this boxing saga.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: “Creed” has its clichés and its big mandatory crowd-pleasing moments, but even they are handled well by a confident filmmaker who is a true rising talent.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Ryan Coogler managed to bring everything that we expect from a Rocky movie but made it feel fresh and authentic. As far as boxing films go, Creed is a masterpiece on so many levels.​
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: Though a smart and superbly shot film, the story structure follows a familiar and predictable trajectory for anyone acquainted with Stallone's original.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Stallone shines once again as the dearly loved Rocky Balboa and hands over the gloves to Michael B. Jordan's Adonis Creed.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: Nevermind all that stuff we maybe once said about forging your own path or being your own man - what really matters is you eventually take your father's name
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: This exhilarating, blood-soaked Rocky spin-off is the first contender for film of the year.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: Proves the blend of boxing and underdogs is still a potent mix, made better by rich performances and Stallone's quietly affecting work.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Creed will make you stand up to cheer and leave you wishing for one more round.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: With all of the redundancies in plot and imagery, it might as well have been one long montage of scenes pulled from the previous six pictures.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Creed hits hardest thanks to a never-better Stallone. Some actors get better with age. Others fade into the distance, taken over by younger talents never to be found again...
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: There's an incredible empowerment in Creed that speaks volumes to our current generation. With Stallone representing the past, he passes on the boxing and life metaphor torch to Michael B. Jordan which he seizes with open arms.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Although the narrative follows the basic pattern of the previous films, Coogler and Jordan infuse it with an identity all its own. There's a level of grit that hasn't been seen since the original.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: The best "Rocky" movie since "Rocky," but it more than stands on it's own merits.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: Being a sequel and spin-off, it rejuvenates the past glory of Rocky's world with a round of good performances from Sylvester Stallone and Michael B. Jordan. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Rocky has always been about heart, and 40 years into the franchise, it would seem there's still plenty to spare.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Cynics could easily latch on to the problems above and dismiss CREED as franchise smelling salts. To do so, however, would be to also dismiss the new talent Coogler and Jordan bring to the creaking joints of the ROCKY brand.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: We're lucky to have Creed. With most franchises, the seventh installment wouldn't even be in theaters, much less worth a damn.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Placing focus on the young Creed allows Jordan to breathe his youthful talents into the film. He successfully carries the weight of being the main focal point.
reviews.author: Phumlani S Langa

reviews.text: Creed goes the distance and then some.
reviews.author: David Harris

reviews.text: [Ryan] Coogler proves to be a great action director with his close, seamless fight shots, while capturing uncheesy sports montages and intimate interactions.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: 'Creed' is not a novelty, but it is different enough from the first installment of the franchise. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Adonis' presence splits the cinematic illusion like a prism, as it hops back and forth between fighters. In one moment, Adonis punches alongside Apollo, embracing his legacy. In the next, he rejects it, fighting Apollo himself.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Creed is a meditation on fatherlessness, a call-to-arms for black youth who are taught lowered expectations to believe they are powerful, a rousing boxing flick, a quality love story, and one of the best damn films of the year.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: What's disappointing about Creed is how slavishly it follows the template of the previous pictures. It's not bad -- it's the best entry since Rocky III -- but one's enjoyment depends entirely on how charitable one is feeling in the nostalgia department.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Director Ryan Coogler gives the film a surprisingly indy feel for such a mainstream franchise.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Ryan Coogler, an accomplished talent after just two films, wisely trades in the authenticity of 'televising' Creed's bouts, a platitudinous technique used so ubiquitously in boxing movies, for intimate handycam...
reviews.author: Christopher Preston

reviews.text: Creed is not just about boxing or the character of Rocky, but about building new relationships and how a name with a legacy can make you or break you, making it difficult to branch out on your own.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: While CREED seems to resemble typical fare, the conflict between these two men of who's fighting for whom clears the smoke. In the end, it's the audience who wins.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: To say the fight scenes are thrilling is an understatement; by the end of the movie, I was in tears. Talk about exceeding expectations.
reviews.author: Bernard Boo

reviews.text: Creed is as gritty and grounded as the original Rocky, and it packs an emotional punch that's as powerful as any in the ring
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: A completed motion picture is a work that represents thousands and thousands of creative decisions. It's remarkable how many of those creative decisions Ryan Coogler and his team got right on Creed.
reviews.author: Ed Travis

reviews.text: This is a crowd-pleasing reboot of the Rocky franchise, with writer/director Ryan Coogler capturing the spirit of the previous films while creating an experience that stands alone.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: In short, it's a knockout.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: I was worried that it would either stick too close to the franchise's winning but tired formula, or go too far in a new direction and alienate the die-hards. Creed stands on its own, and as a lifelong fan, I am happy to stand behind it.
reviews.author: Di Golding

reviews.text: Creed is perfect. This moment is perfect. I hope Creed II is anywhere near as intoxicating.
reviews.author: Shea Serrano

reviews.text: Coogler proves a true dab hand at mining the rich backstory of the Rocky universe to fashion a surprisingly tasteful take on its characters, themes and overall conventions.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Creed is less a continuation of the Rocky story and more of a new beginning within the same universe; similar in narrative and theme, but built for a new generation.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: For those of you who grew up on these movies, think of it as revisiting an old friend who may not be around much longer. And meeting a new friend with a bright future.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: Coogler spins and remixes the original Rocky montages and symbolism into Creed's boxing Bildungsroman, balancing the tenuous struggle between fan service and personality.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: I don't watch boxing but I was fascinated by every moment of the film because it pulled me in. It made me care.
reviews.author: Erik Anderson

reviews.text: As a pitch, this might have led to the gloopiest Philly cheesesteak ever, but what do you know - it's a knockout.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: Creed is a filmmaker's film and, at the same time, a well crafted everyman story and audience pleaser.
reviews.author: Lapacazo Magrira Sandoval

reviews.text: Well-crafted, exciting, funny, and inspiring, and it's successful in being original by not trying too hard to be original.
reviews.author: Jordan Calhoun

reviews.text: The savvy, intelligence, and heart of director Ryan Coogler's screenplay equals his achievement in getting an assignment like this after making Fruitvale Station in Oakland at age 26.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: They way it's shot, particularly with the fighting scenes, is very raw. You feel like you're in the ring. There were a couple times where I almost ducked.
reviews.author: Andre Meadows

reviews.text: It's a lovely performance, with Stallone using his age and size and slow way of talking to guide the retired, lonely Rocky, while Jordan is the anxious, ambitious Adonis Johnson, the son of Apollo Creed...
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: A positive act of cultural appropriation...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: ... Creed transits between nostalgia and promise, and is more entertaining than substantial. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: Creed is a triumph at expanding on the legacy of many beloved characters, and a film that can stand on its own two feet
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Simply put, if you like films about boxing, with the emotional quotient thrown in, you will enjoy this one. It's Stallone, after all.
reviews.author: Reagan Gavin Rasquinha

reviews.text: The initial pace is on the slow side and the story teeters between drama and melodrama, but the boxing sequences are excellent, and Coogler builds an unstoppable momentum. Welcome back, Rocky.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Creed is flawless-they ought to teach it in film school.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Creed certainly looks like a reboot-spinoff, but without the crass cash-grab feeling we've come to expect from such fare. Don't call it a franchise comeback, because Creed is something else altogether.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: While a little unsteady at first, Creed soars midway and the final act is a knockout.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: This was one of my favorite surprises of the year.
reviews.author: Brooke Corso

reviews.text: Creed is Rocky's movie. Same as it ever was.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: It's a film with almost uniformly strong performances.
reviews.author: Arthur Gies

reviews.text: Creed could easily become the foundation for a franchise, allowing Sylvester Stallone to age gracefully and take up less space on the screen, while still conveying that punch-drunk wisdom.
reviews.author: Peter Walsh

reviews.text: Sylvester Stallone gives the most compelling and truthful performance of his career.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: The movie as a whole is still excellent and well worth seeking out -- even if you don't really care about boxing or Rocky.
reviews.author: Lesley Coffin

reviews.text: Creed is a film that respects the Rocky franchise, made by someone who seems to have a genuine love for the franchise and understands why people loved the very first film.
reviews.author: Alex Lines

reviews.text: Stallone is not only giving his best performance to since Rocky, but Michael B. Jordan has fully established himself as a leading man to be reckoned with.
reviews.author: Wilson Morales

reviews.text: Adonis and Rocky make one of the year's best cinematic pairings, their transition from strangers to acquaintances to partners to friends to something so much more absolutely exquisite.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Creed is a special film that pound for pound competes with the best heartstring-pulling of Rocky Balboa's 40-year screen odyssey but, crucially, looks to what's ahead in a very exciting way.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: Simply put, Creed is a total triumph.
reviews.author: Ben Rawson-Jones

reviews.text: Creed is feels gritty and lived in, while also hitting technical highs like an astonishing single-take boxing match. It's funny and sweet and sad and scrappy. You never saw this one coming.
reviews.author: Tara Thorne

reviews.text: It's a formula film, executed to near perfection. And it wields a secret weapon: our nostalgia for the original.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Creed stands tall as one of the most entertaining sports films we've seen in years; a scintillating and, occasionally, moving piece with genuine heart, energy, depth and humour. Oh, and the fight scenes are brilliant.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: Sure, this being Philly there's fair dollop of cheese with that steak. But Creed still packs a surprising punch.
reviews.author: Russell Baillie

reviews.text: Creed is a franchise-reinvigorating reboot that can hold its own alongside a very select few.
reviews.author: Vicky Roach

reviews.text: 'Creed's' the kind of gritty, cozy, workaday tale we love in America, with more than a little in common with the hugely popular, also Philly-based MMA fight-film, 'Warrior.'
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Its own great, singular achievement, outside of the considerable iconography.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Coogler and company get the essence of "Rocky," from the Italian Stallion's rambling, close-mouthed monologues to the woodwind and horn-based score to the cornball montages.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: While it makes the bold move of turning Rocky into a supporting character, this solid slice of mainstream entertainment will please fans of the long-running boxing series.
reviews.author: Richard James Havis

reviews.text: Like a palooka charging from his corner, Creed plunges ahead with only a few sidesteps. (Director) Coogler takes his time with each development, endearing these already likable characters to the viewer even more.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: Creed is that rarest of things: a standalone film with real emotional punch and thematic complexity that also continues and expands upon a very well-established, now almost cliché franchise.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: An honest film the will thrill the thoughest and that can be enjoyed even by those who haven't seen the originals. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Carlos Berner

reviews.text: Director Ryan Coogler proves to be a filmmaker with a great capacity for narrative, and just like his character, he's trying to leave more than a good impression - a legacy. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Israel Acosta Aroche

reviews.text: with Creed, the series really has returned to its roots... there's an earthiness and street quality that we haven't witnessed since the 1976 original.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: This is everything we could have hoped for from a Rocky spinoff and more. It's a story about legacy, race, purpose, trust, and friendship.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: Creed is able to succeed as an exceptionally entertaining sports story, and the groundwork for building an identity free from the past.
reviews.author: Michael Snydel

reviews.text: Stallone delivers a touching and wonderfully understated performance.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: A powerful drama with great fight sequences and a superb camera work. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Díaz Reyes

reviews.text: The most romantic story in sports films the industry has ever contributed to pop culture. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Arturo Aguilar

reviews.text: Creed may not reunite generations like Star Wars did, but has fiber and muscle to keep fighting. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Creed reimagined a classic, while paying tribute to a character that remains after forty years. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Krauze

reviews.text: In this revival, there is not only talent, but also affection and intelligence. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Costa

reviews.text: Coogler manages to make one of the best films in the series showing a Rocky full of courage and elegance. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: While this film is basically Rocky VII, it's also much more than that, and perhaps the best in the series as it tells a standalone story with energy and skill.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: The plot is pretty simple, but it has a good start and a clear end, also has moments that easily remind us to Rocky(1976). [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jonathan Sánchez

reviews.text: A powerfull, emotional and well told story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Edgardo Reséndiz

reviews.text: Sylvester Stallone reminds us why we fell in love with Rocky in the first place. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Eduardo Molina

reviews.text: If Rocky was a K.O, Creed is a T.K.O.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: The most beloved fighter in cinema does not stand anymore in the ring. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Arce

reviews.text: It has enough original (and strange) elements to feel like its own entity and stand out. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Every round in this film is a knockout and it overall lives up to the franchise. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Adrián Ruiz

reviews.text: A serious treatment of the story of a young man trying to get out of his abscent father's shadow. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Ortiz

reviews.text: Coogler draws on the traditional elements of Rocky's success - strength of character in adversity, old-fashioned romance and, of course, a climactic fight - and tricks them out for the mobile phone generation to give them a new lease of life.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Creed feeds itself from nostalgia and offers a brand new vehicule to the young audience. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Abuín

reviews.text: A heavyweight in every sense that will keep you hooked from gritty start to celebratory finish.
reviews.author: Rob Carnevale

reviews.text: Coogler, as shown in his film debut Fruitvale Station, shows his capacity to create an intimate drama and set the stage for a new icon in film boxing. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: Coogler excels in his narrative with great storytelling and doses of humor in a story we all know, while inducing a "realness" factor into the typical sports movie melodrama (no easy task). [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oscar Uriel

reviews.text: An utter accomplishment that works as a part of Rocky Balboa's tale, and as the beginning of a new underdog saga.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Any fan of the saga that doesn't feel the sweat in his eyes when seeing this film is simply dead inside. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Uriel Barco

reviews.text: It's amazing how hollywod keeps bringing back sagas, however, this time it feels like the new generation of filmmakers can surpass the originals. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: It's not necessary to be a fan of the Rocky saga to enjoy this film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rodrigo Rivera

reviews.text: Exciting and introspective, Creed is one of the best films of the Rocky saga. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: César Albarrán Torres

reviews.text: So exciting it will make you want to go see it again immediately, something very rare these days. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Benítez

reviews.text: Is it cheesy? Hell yes, but that's to be expected, and Creed manages to be utterly fantastic at the same time.
reviews.author: Andrew Pollard

reviews.text: Creed is a sure-fire hit that's impossible to hate but I may have to punch the next person who tells me it made them cry.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Coogler is skilled at stoking nostalgia while delivering something that feels both fresh and funny.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: A terrific surprise of a film.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: Coogler and Jordan bring an authenticity and intelligence that elevates Creed from the restrictions of a franchise movie.
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: What follows may be familiar fare, but Coogler somehow manages to revivify the series, aided by a punchy turn from Jordan and deceptively complex support from Tessa Thompson ...
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Surprisingly thoughtful and stylish.
reviews.author: Jason Anderson

reviews.text: A shot of box-fresh blood.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: A fresh-faced crowd-pleaser as smart and informed in the story's lore as it is rousing for Rocky fans and the uninitiated alike.
reviews.author: Karen Krizanovich

reviews.text: [Coogler] directs with muscular assurance, confident enough to deploy the old one-two combo of violence in the ring and sentiment outside the ropes.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Aside from continuing the Rocky story in a hugely satisfying manner, Creed also stands as an immensely enjoyable boxing movie in its own right.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: If you can stomach the schmaltz and suspend your disbelief in the face of the film's pounding predictability, you'll find plenty to enjoy.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Stallone impresses most of all. Maybe it is time to hang up his Expendables gun and leave the elderly action-man stuff behind.
reviews.author: Alex Zane

reviews.text: It's absorbing stuff.
reviews.author: Greg O'Keefe

reviews.text: The Rocky franchise long ago seemed to be on the ropes, but here, fully 40 years after the original, comes the seventh film in the series, and I'm pleased to report that it packs a genuine dramatic punch.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: This add-on to the Rocky franchise boasts a comparably deft mix of crowd-pleasing familiarity and freshness, particularly in the shape of its canny new casting - a combination that's set to excite a new generation of fans.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: It's a relief to watch this likable boxing picture, which finds a way to evolve the Rocky franchise with humour and humility.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Director Ryan Coogler knows exactly when to hit us with a training montage or an emotional speech, but he also throws some unexpected punches.
reviews.author: Jamie Dunn

reviews.text: Coogler brings renewed energy to a four decades-old franchise. [Full review in Portuguese.]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Creed is as good as the original Rocky (seriously).
reviews.author: Alex Leadbeater

reviews.text: Harking back to the franchise's glory days, it's a movie hardcore Rocky fans will love.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: From the perfectly judged poignancy to the beautifully choreographed and brutal bouts, Creed certainly goes the distance.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: Subtly, smartly, writer-director Ryan Coogler bobs and weaves around racial identity even as this Rocky 2.0 expertly does what it's been coached to do--belt us with one bruising, pulsating boxing movie.
reviews.author: Brian Gibson

reviews.text: To call Creed the best Rocky movie since the original might seem faint praise to those who reflexively deride the sequels; it is in many ways a better-made movie than the somewhat rough-hewn Rocky.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: Following the failure of the underrated Rocky Balboa, the Rocky series was on the canvas, the count nearing ten. Creed not only gets it - and Sly Stallone - back on its feet, but completely reinvigorates it.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt (UK)

reviews.text: Creed is part of a new (or should that be old?) wave of thinly disguised remakes masquerading as post-modern sequels to the iconic hits of yesteryear.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: Ryan Coogler's sequel follows a "Rocky" road
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Creed isn't complicated. It's a simple story with just enough humanity sprinkled throughout to capture the hearts and minds of audiences who -- trust me when I say this -- will be cheering at the end.
reviews.author: David Blaustein

reviews.text: Stallone enjoys inspired chemistry with co-star Michael B. Jordan... and Ryan Coogler directs the hell out of the movie.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: One of the best films of the Rocky series, worthy of the championship belt.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: I love this movie. I do.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Coogler infuses his film with a genuine passion and unironic attachment to the original's best qualities, particularly its delicate balancing act between anguish and triumph
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Irksomely epic in its dreariness and cheesiness, this is nevertheless a film that will appeal to the converted.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: The smartest thing Sylvester Stallone did was to not write and/or direct this film. Ryan Coogler brings a fresh set of eyes to the project. Creed works both as part of a larger franchise and on its own massively entertaining terms.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The surest sign that Coogler has honored his source material is that Creed is populist through and through. His achievement... is that he gives his audience exactly what they want and makes it feel like a gift rather than a bribe.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: I'm not afraid to say that Stallone could earn some award consideration for his work here.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: Everyone is deserving of credit, but the holy trinity at play here is Coogler, Jordan, and Stallone.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: With a loving look to the past and a confident glance towards the future, Creed is a triumphant entry in the Rocky franchise. This is Rocky V done right.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Along with Sicario, this has to be one of the most impressively shot movies of the year.
reviews.author: Ron Yamauchi

reviews.text: Rocky fans will recognise the many cues and nods to Balboa's previous adventures (including the iconic Philadelphia Steps sequence), and the 69-year-old Stallone gives one of his most affectionate performances.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Creed manages to rise above its well-worn premise and deliver a film that is at once stylish, engaging and ultimately moving.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: There's a chance that Creed might have turned out just fine without Coogler at the helm. But that version of Creed would lack the chief detail that makes Coogler's film so good: perspective.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: Writer-director Ryan Coogler ('Fruitvale Station') serves notice in this film that he is one of the best young writer-directors around. He shows a sure hand directing exciting boxing scenes, as well as convincing romantic and dramatic scenes.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Creed proves just good enough to be disappointing.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: Anyone hoping the franchise might open out into new thematic territory will be disappointed; this is the same old ritual, from the amped-up training sequences to the climactic title fight with its absurd number of punches landed in every round.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: Hey, Stallone does it again. Don't worry about it.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Coogler has carried off some astonishing set pieces in Creed, including a two-round prizefight shot in a single, continuously mobile take. The scene would have been impressive had it been only a stunt; but like all true acts of cinema, it's more.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Coogler directed Jordan in the powerful Fruitvale Station, and he knows what he has in this actor.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Normally it would annoy me to see a movie that is such a blatant copy, but in this case, Creed feels more like an apology for the mediocre Rocky movies we've endured.
reviews.author: Alex Falcone

reviews.text: The title itself -- with 'Creed' replacing 'Rocky' -- is significant: It's a recognition of America's changing demography, and a rebuke to the movie industry's flimsy excuses for its diversity problem.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Jordan and Stallone trade great moments through muffled feelings and half-spoken sentences, ensuring we never feel the manipulative hand of Hollywood sliding up their boxers. The movie is subtle in many of the places it could have been obvious..
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: Creed is superior popular entertainment that shows that a mass audience can be electrified by a film that does not rely on elaborate set-pieces or complicated special effects.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Despite being a bit too long, Creed reveals Coogler as a solid writer and director. He manages to remain true to his indie roots while working on a mainstream Hollywood film.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: The best Rocky movie since the original.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: The rapport between Stallone and Jordan is fabulous, especially in the old-school training scenes, chasing chickens to improve speed and all the rest, that pay homage to the original, Oscar-winning 1976 film.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Creed moves the Rocky franchise into the present and gives it a future; Coogler makes the story his own, even as he pays respect to what has gone before.
reviews.author: Philippa Hawker

reviews.text: One of the joys of Creed is seeing Rocky at peace. It's been a long time since Stallone was allowed to play a character who could listen rather than fight, who could be rather than do.
reviews.author: Kenneth R. Morefield

reviews.text: Creed packs a serious punch, replete with crunching fight sequences captured in a probing, prowling style.
reviews.author: Ashley Clark

reviews.text: At its core it's just another sports movie - and hell, a Part 7, no less - but there's a strong and sincere foundation that works resoundingly well.
reviews.author: Scott Weinberg

reviews.text: It's got a terrific fight at the end, and all the proceeding stuff is professional and clear, while never being thrilling or surprising ... [a shot of a turtle is] the most blatant and risible phallic symbol I've seen in a movie in a long time.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: I felt like I'd gone 12 rounds with someone who recited bad poetry while hitting me with a wet sock.
reviews.author: Tim Martain

reviews.text: "Creed" is a tremendous movie that overcomes what might have been the longest odds of all - injecting some prestige back into the "Rocky" franchise.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: It's an invigorating piece of nostalgia that fuels a bigger adrenaline rush with its climax than any big-budget blockbuster could provide.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Jordan is mighty fine as the young self-taught fighter with self worth issues, but it's the old action star, slipping right back into his creation's skin with humility and humor, who is "Creed's" beating heart.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Big-budget, studio-produced franchise films don't get any better than this.
reviews.author: Daniel Gelb

reviews.text: ...a decent Rocky followup that could (and should) have been so much better (ie the movie is longer than any of the six preceding installments).
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: 'Creed' is a winner.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Feels natural and organic, not forced by the dictates of movie franchises. A smart, engaging, unsentimental portrait of male friendship and male emotion.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: 'Creed' has the heart of a champion, and provides the modern updating necessary to give the 'Rocky' franchise a new lease on life.
reviews.author: Mark Hughes

reviews.text: By taking all the good will that was originally generated when "Rocky" won the Oscar for best picture and combining that with what little credibility remains in the character, Coogler packages together a tender, exciting and respectful film.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: It is as much about us, and our association with this nearly 40-year series, as it is about its characters.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: It's hokey, it's predictable and, if you're a fan, it's surprisingly engaging. A big reason is that Stallone-often an underrated actor -underplays the role.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: Heartfelt, respectful franchise extender...The film chiefly uses the events of Rocky III as foreshadowing for this well-thought over story...It's very difficult to imagine anyone with even a passing interest in the Rocky films not enjoying Creed.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: This film doesn't mark a continuation of the series. It marks a rebirth of it. One of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: John Hanlon

reviews.text: The 7th Rocky movie looks pretty much like all the rest but it's so much fun and always a real treat to see Sly Stallone do his most famous character.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: The name on the title card may have changed, but the Rocky legacy is alive and thriving in Creed.
reviews.author: Kofi Outlaw

reviews.text: Don't call it a comeback; the Rocky movies have been here for years.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: The journey of Adonis Creed covers the same ground, but it all feels vital again thanks to extraordinary directorial care and an interest in revisiting the world of Rocky Balboa from a fresh angle.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Coogler keeps everything moving so gracefully that by the end of Creed, we almost don't know what hit us.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Whether the credit goes to the director or the actor or both, this is the performance of Stallone's career, one in which that age-defying orange body stays covered up but his sadness is in full view.
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: Creed delivers predictable uplift but, ultimately, fails to make a unique name for itself.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Creed attempts to create a new mythology (read: franchise) around a young boxer, the very fit Michael B. Jordan, by manufacturing cheap affection for a ghost of cinema past.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Edalatpour

reviews.text: ...a great balance of tender character moments and electric boxing-related events.
reviews.author: Jon Winkler

reviews.text: Ryan takes advantage of the fact Stallone is a solid character actor who got waylaid into stardom.
reviews.author: Kirk Honeycutt

reviews.text: Don't think of Creed as Rocky VII. Think of it as an addition to the house Balboa built.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: CREED goes the distance, and is the best ROCKY movie since the original.
reviews.author: Devin Faraci

reviews.text: The Oakland-born filmmaker Ryan Coogler has worked more miracles with the 40 year-old Rocky series.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Doing some deft shadow boxing with the increasingly wheezy, cheesy Rocky legacy, Coogler honours its 1976 roots -- getting some poignant support from Sylvester Stallone -- while giving the franchise some relevant, rousing 21st-century direction.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: What Hollywood director would make a movie in which the hero braids his girlfriend's hair or confides to her his fear of failure?
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: We knew Creed was always a worthy opponent, but we never expected Creed to be such a worthy sequel/spin-off movie.
reviews.author: John Gholson

reviews.text: A familiar story that speaks to people of any age...'Creed' is fulfilling, crowd-pleasing, entertainment...
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Creed is a movie that plays to type and presses a lot of emotional buttons, and it does it so well that you just might forget to rail against formula and cheer for the underdog once more.
reviews.author: Alex Doenau

reviews.text: The film is full of life and loose humor, and Creed often transcends the genre by playing with movie mythology.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Hot damn! Fruitvale Station director Coogler, 29, turbocharges the Rocky franchise. Jordan is stellar. And so irresistible is Stallone's blend of tough and tender that Oscar should give him points. Yo, Academy!
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Not even Rocky can deliver a line like, "It's you against you; he's just in the ring" without sounding ridiculous
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Adonis Creed is an American hero audiences could adore for a long time. He climbed the Rocky Steps right next to the Italian Stallion himself. What else is he capable of?
reviews.author: Kwame Opam

reviews.text: 'Creed' is a winner and a sublime achievement that all audiences are going to love.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: It's a hell of a movie, a funny mix of corn and street: street corn.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: A winning, heartfelt story.... The best Rocky film since the first one.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Creed works better as an actual movie than it does as a Rocky movie, which is quite the compliment, considering that it's an excellent Rocky movie, too.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: What a welcome surprise to find that Creed is so good, so satisfying that it gives Rocky -- and up-by-the-bootstraps sagas, in general -- a good name again.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: It is not for me to reveal whether the skirmish will last its allotted 12 rounds. However, you should know it is 120 times the spectacle of that flippin' awful Mayweather-Pacquiao farce.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Creed stirs emotions with a strong yet artful hand.
reviews.author: John Wenzel

reviews.text: Creed isn't a complete TKO, but it goes all 12 rounds with vitality and flourish.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: The best "Rocky" film since the original. Stallone is Oscar caliber. Jordan is a star.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: If you're up for an homage to Rocky, then ding-ding, "Creed" answers the bell.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: At his best, his new film is both visually striking and expressive: those lightning opening vignettes, for example, convey the volatile, claustrophobic tensions of juvie in mere seconds.
reviews.author: Michael Sragow

reviews.text: Coogler manages to breathe enough new life into this offering to make it seem fresh and even new to a degree. (Full Content Review - Sex, Profanity, Violence, etc. - for Parents also available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: ... Hits many of the same story beats as the original "Rocky" but is very much its own entity, introducing a compelling new character and taking an old favorite into the most dramatically rich terrain he's encountered.
reviews.author: Greg Maki

reviews.text: Feel-good boxing drama is both a hit and a miss.
reviews.author: S. Jhoanna Robledo

reviews.text: It's fascinating to see Stallone hand over his franchise to a Black director and Black lead, especially in an era where films are being whitewashed and movie studios still refusing to accept the buying power of African-American audiences.
reviews.author: Clay Cane

reviews.text: Yo, Sly! You might wanna practice that Oscar speech, the one you originally wrote back in 1976.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: If you don't feel a thrill when, during that championship bout, the original "Rocky" theme suddenly kicks in, I can't help you.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: There's a lot to like and more to love about this movie, but most of it comes down to Jordan, whose performance as Adonis is raw and rousing, and to Stallone, who at 69 does some of his best acting in years.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: While passable, everything in Creed feels calculated
reviews.author: Willie Waffle

reviews.text: "Creed" packs a mighty punch.
reviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz

reviews.text: A movie that reminds us why we loved the original, made by people who obviously cherish it as much as we do.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Creed is the first Rocky sequel that feels like the first Rocky. It's human-scaled, rambling and idiosyncratic, with emotional payoffs larger than life. I spent most of the running time crying my eyes out.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Coogler and co-writer Aaron Covington gracefully blend familiar elements of the Rocky franchise with a more contemporary look at a boxer's life.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: A fascinating remix, it amazes by doing the unexpected in a sub-genre that's fatiguing with its dedication to formula.
reviews.author: Cameron Williams

reviews.text: As fun, stylish and gripping as the actual fights are, the charms in Creed are found in the interaction between Rocky and Adonis.
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: Cooger adds a few visual flourishes -- a fire eater appears in a darkened arena; Philly youth pull wheelies on their motor bikes -- that give Creed a bit of new style, but mainly the movie is same old same old.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: Like the sport of boxing itself, the luster of the Rocky movies has faded over time. But Rocky Balboa has always been Stallone's achievement. It's a joy to spend a little more time with him, even if he's a little older and slower.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: One of the year's warmest and most crowd-pleasing surprises.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: Creed is a rare kind of franchise film. It pays homage to the first movie in the series but ultimately manages to step out of its shadow and stand on its own.
reviews.author: Sam Watermeier

reviews.text: Despite getting laid out in excruciatingly graphic detail, the kid somehow comes roaring back, not so much struggling to his feet as leaping. Which is exactly what this energetic, hugely entertaining film does for the four-decades-old franchise.
reviews.author: Tom Russo

reviews.text: Reprising the role that made him famous, Stallone turns in an award-worthy performance in the Rocky reboot Creed. He doesn't overplay things; he's downright humble and, let's face it, kind of adorable.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: Rather than going through the motions of the Rocky tradition one more time, it's an honest-to-goodness movie, one that contains some serious artistry (Fox29 Philly)
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Neither fans nor those new to the Rocky legend will be disappointed with what writer director Ryan Cooglar has done with Stallone's characters in what is probably his last appearance
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: The seventh "Rocky" film is uneven but gets by on Jordan's charisma and some stunning fight sequences.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: True to the Rocky tradition but bringing it forward.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Within the inevitable boundaries of a venerable franchise, Coogler and company do fine work convincing us against our better judgment that nothing we see is preordained, that anything can happen within the four corners of the ring.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: The themes of love, loyalty, ambition, honor and legacy that lend sinew to the story are delivered with such a clean punch that they as feel as fresh as they did in 1976.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: It's surprising proof that iconic franchises that started in the 1970s can be revived in all the right ways. "Star Wars" fans, take note.
reviews.author: Jeff Baker

reviews.text: I feared signing on to Creed might derail Coogler's and Jordan's careers. Instead, this revitalizing crowd-pleaser solidifies my belief that these two have the potential to create really great art.
reviews.author: Aisha Harris

reviews.text: Often, extending a movie franchise signifies a lack of imagination. But "Creed" is a knockout.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: Stallone can't let go of the spotlight, even though he barely has a handle on his own character. His Balboa has been Xeroxed too many times; he's all blurry around the edges.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Creed cares about these men as much as they care about each other. That comes through loud and clear, with a gut-punch degree of poignancy.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: "Creed" is a dandy piece of entertainment, soothingly old-fashioned and bracingly up-to-date.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: If the plot of "Creed" echoes the original "Rocky," at least it's echoing something worthwhile. But there are differences.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: All eyes are on Jordan and rightly so, but Stallone also earns his place, reprising the downbeat, lovable lug from Rocky Balboa who struggled to get past emotional and physical blocks for one last shot at a title.
reviews.author: Linda Barnard

reviews.text: What makes Creed work as well as it does is the same thing that made the first Rocky the sleeper hit it was in 1976; writer Aaron Covington and writer/director Ryan Coogler give as much attention to what goes on outside the ring as within it.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Creed is not just a knockout boxing movie, it coaxes Rocky Balboa off the mat and revives an iconic American hero.
reviews.author: Bruce Kirkland

reviews.text: Manages to both satisfy fans and toy with expectations, twisting many of the clichés that Rocky helped propagate in order to craft a new bout of pugilism. Easily one of the best films of the season.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: ... easily Stallone's career-best performance, although honestly the bar was never set that high.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: We can all only hope that we'll get to see Adonis on screen for just as long as we've seen Rocky.
reviews.author: Josh Lasser

reviews.text: a performance from Jordan that has the emotional urgency and fluid grace of a perfectly delivered left hook.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Creed is a reboot of the franchise and follows a very similar structure to the original movie. To that end, the movie repeatedly falls short.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Creed is the happiest surprise of the movie season, a mix of old and new that taps our reservoir of nostalgia and forges a path of its own. It serves comfort food with fresh ingredients.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: Coogler knows what Stallone has always known: It's not about the fights. It's about making an audience feel deeply about the people involved in the fights.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Creed understands the value of formulas and of archetypes, but more importantly, it knows how to push off them to find the unexpected. It feels familiar, as it should, but it is also, in its own right, electrifying.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: The sleeper hit of the year. If you're not on your feet cheering by the end, check your pulse. You might be dead.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: It doesn't muster the pure underdog audacity of the first "Rocky," but it does pair some exceptional actors with engaging characters.
reviews.author: Jon Niccum

reviews.text: Creed is a crowd-pleasing, franchise-extending nostalgia trip of the rarest sort: one that's not just enjoyable but inspired.
reviews.author: Sam Woolf

reviews.text: By contending with the unglamorous nature of professionally beating other people into unconsciousness, the film makes more time for its characters' inner lives.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: Creed is formulaic and predictable, but it's also joyful and wise and tinged with lament, and it lands on the sweet spot between heartfelt art and mainstream entertainment too many Hollywood studios don't even try to hit.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: The incredible Sylvester Stallone, now 69, carries himself like a man who has been physically bruised and emotionally battered yet deep down remains a fighter.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: Creed reinvigorates the Rocky franchise while remaining true in both tone and spirit to the original film in a way that's both engaging and satisfying.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Coogler has created an energizing addition to the Rocky series that doesn't just succeed as a respectful passing of the torch, but as one of the best Rocky movies ever made.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: With a deftly crafted blend of smarts and corn - of course there's corn, people, this is Rocky! - it earns our trust: It's gonna go right to the edge with the heartstring-tugging, but it won't go over.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: Stallone has not only taken a risk on Coogler but submitted to a personal sea change. And when those trumpets do blare, a new actor emerges.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: As Creed's rough-hewn boxer Donnie "Adonis" Johnson (née Creed), Jordan is granted another career-making role by [Ryan] Coogler.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: As Weathers might have said on Arrested Development: Toughness, feeling, solid action, good performances: You got yourself a stew, man.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Creed is an echo. It's a call back to every other Rocky movie, and while it's good, it can't create separation from the powerful legacy of the Rocky series.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: A moving final round for Stallone's most enduring creation.
reviews.author: Jon Lyus

reviews.text: The movie's tropes are comforting in their familiarity. The tale of a decent hero fighting long odds never gets old.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: Time adds layers to stories. What was a plot device for Rocky IV now paved the way for the story of a son's struggle for identity, forgiveness and allows him to make an impact on a legend.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Do not miss this film. It's the best in the franchise since 1976.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Equally powerful and feel-good, Creed is an entertaining reminder that this franchise isn't down for the count yet.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Creed leaves all doubts flat on the mat. It's a rousing, crowd-pleasing blast of entertainment that is not only a well-made sports movie but is also a soulful, cinematic love letter to Philadelphia, the city that has become synonymous with Rocky Balboa.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Once again, I find myself saying if this is the last time we see Rocky Balboa, it's a worthy encore.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: And yet the film is not only the franchise's most visually dynamic, it's an emotional powerhouse that recaptures everything that made "Rocky" great.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Proves that there's life in the old Italian Stallion yet...if you doubted that the 'Rocky' franchise could use still another episode, 'Creed' should make you a believer.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: 'Rocky' and the next Roman numeral might not be in the title, but this engaging and faithful seventh episode includes all the fixins for a highly-recommended spin-off of the storied franchise.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: This is one of the best films of 2015.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: In "Creed," "Rocky" finally has a worthy successor. For many reasons.
reviews.author: Tony Hicks

reviews.text: Creed works far better than it should, and does so twice: as the unexpected payoff to a nearly 40-year-old series, and as the confirmation of a major talent in its director.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: [G]o-for-broke range of emotions, dealing with ambition, talent, legacy, romance... Stallone? At his minimalist best as a man of the streets, shouldering years of quiet living: where has this fine actor been hiding these recent years?
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: It's [director Ryan] Coogler's personal touches and vision that elevate Creed from the ordinary.
reviews.author: Daniel Eagan

reviews.text: Questionable as a film (sparring with formula), good as a movie, and brilliant as a franchise-extender. It's shameless, near-surgically effective cross-generational corn for guys.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: When the usual franchise tropes are busted out they're done in a way that's filtered through a new voice.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: The burly backstory and weight of personal history don't stall the drama but provide its fuel.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: 2015 has seen its share of sequels; perhaps surprisingly, Creed is among the best.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Don't go assuming this is just another undercard in the Rocky series. After a somewhat predictable start, Ryan Coogler digs in to deliver what is undeniably a hit to the heart: the most emotionally satisfying crescendo of the year.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Creed is corny like the old Rocky films, but riveting like the old Rocky films, too.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: The great irony of Ryan Coogler's Creed is that it is among the more grounded entries in the Rocky series yet acts as a direct sequel to the ultra-fantastical Rocky IV.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: Ryan Coogler accomplished what would have seemed impossible 40 years ago: He got the audience to chant "Creed!" in a Rocky movie.
reviews.author: Justin Gerber

reviews.text: This seventh film in the Rocky series sticks to the creed they all do: it knows how well the formula works, what's needed to reinvigorate it, and gets the whole apparatus pumping as well here as it has in a generation.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Albeit familiar, Sylvester Stallone in this redemptive, crowd-pleasing spinoff could even be a Best Supporting Actor Oscar contender. Wouldn't that be a knockout punch?
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: With "Creed," Coogler proves he is one of the most skillful young directors around. Turns out we really did need another "Rocky" movie. It just needed to keep Rocky in perspective, and in proportion.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: There is nothing bad about Creed, but there is nothing special that makes it stand out. It is literally a beat-for-beat reboot of the original Rocky.
reviews.author: Alyse Wax

reviews.text: Rousing in spirit, surprisingly emotional and visually dynamic, filmmaker Ryan Coogler's first studio movie is a worthy successor to the 'Rocky' movies.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: A darn fine boxing movie that pays tribute to the Rocky legacy in a way that fans of those movies should thoroughly enjoy.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: With apologies to Clubber Lang and Ivan Drago, Ryan Coogler's rousingly emotional new film is the best installment since the 1976 original.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: That one-two punch of expectations - energizing a franchise and burnishing the acclaim heaped upon Fruitvale Station - seems to have gotten the best of Ryan Coogler, so that Creed emerges as a reverent entry but never a truly refreshed one.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: Although highlighted by Michael B. Jordan's formidable charisma, "Creed" is only sporadically compelling, resulting in a movie that never quite shakes the impression that it's a novel but not particularly necessary addition to the Rocky series.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Adonis Creed is fighting under the shadow of his father's legacy. Creed is fighting against the legacy of the Rocky sequels. In the end, Creed is a true champion.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Not only lives up to the best of its predecessors, but also respectfully forges its own path.
reviews.author: Andrew Barker

reviews.text: The film keeps pounding through the predictable set-up and storyline until finally, when you think it can fight no longer and will have to throw in the towel, it charges back with some scenes of originality, pathos and, in ever-so-swift jabs, excitement.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Coogler makes the transition from the indie world to big-budget studio filmmaking with a result that's sturdy and smooth. Buffed into ring-ready shape, Jordan acquits himself well both in and out of the ring ...
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: An old franchise flies high again.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

synopsis: Adonis Johnson (Michael B. Jordan) never knew his famous father, boxing champion Apollo Creed, who died before Adonis was born. However, boxing is in his blood, so he seeks out Rocky Balboa (Sylvester Stallone) and asks the retired champ to be his trainer. Rocky sees much of Apollo in Adonis, and agrees to mentor him, even as he battles an opponent deadlier than any in the ring. With Rocky's help, Adonis soon gets a title shot, but whether he has the true heart of a fighter remains to be seen.
